W1 (mechanism), after E012.

The setup
- The tip is E010: E008 (Muon on the conv filters, Lookahead/EMA, resizing 24/28/32 at 40/30/30%, batch 2000, 9.5 nominal epochs, 238 steps) with group 3 narrowed to 512 channels.
- It scores 6.639 s and 0.75477, a margin of 0.18 pp over 0.753.
- E012 reran the tip bit-identically. It reports no held-out seed data, so whether seeds 0-2 sit high is still open.

Measured effects
- Compile + fused SGD: −14% time, deterministic accuracy (E003 = E004 to the digit; E010 = E012).
- Lookahead/EMA: +0.97 pp at about 0.6% time (E005).
- LR floor 0.07 → 0: −0.08 pp. It is redundant with the EMA anneal (E009).
- Muon: +0.66 pp at +4% time (E006).
- Resizing 24/28/32: −22% time, −0.59 pp (E007).
- 0.5 epoch cut: −0.18 pp, −4.8% time (E008).
- Width 576 → 512: −4.8% time, −0.25 pp (E010).
- Resizing with a 20 px stage (E011): −22% time, −0.97 pp. At 20 px the group-3 maps shrink to 2×2, so features degrade much faster than FLOPs fall. Resolution has hit its floor.

The time model
- Fixed cost is about 0.4 s: H2D copy, eigh, pad, the per-epoch 25-way masked-copy augment (host syncs), and the interpolate.
- The variable part is about 6.2 s, GPU-bound at about 26 ms per step. The Muon update is already compiled and its lr is a GPU tensor. The SGD lr is a Python float on the fused SGD, which is outside the compile, so it causes no recompiles.
- Systems-only levers (CUDA graphs, removing graph breaks, folding the augment into the compiled region) are worth 0-4% at most. Max-autotune variants risk slowdowns or memory-pool blowup across 3 resolutions (E003-style).
- Real time tracks pixel share slightly better than linearly.

The accuracy model
- Effects of averaging and optimizer changes are larger than my priors (E005, E006). Simple dial effects (epochs, width) land near the central forecast.
- Muon renormalizes the conv weights and its update has no weight decay term. So weight decay acts only on the BN biases and the head, and "halving wd" for Muon is a no-op; expect ±0.2 pp.
- Muon lr sets the angular step size. A ×1.5 change with 238 steps and EMA damping could move accuracy either way by about 0.3 pp; slightly negative is likely.
- The Lookahead reset damps the variance of the fast weights. A plain EMA with a short final window (about 20 steps) probably loses 0.1-0.5 pp.
- Exchange rates for buying time with accuracy: about 0.36 pp per 10% time (epochs), about 0.5 pp per 10% (width), and about 0.27 pp per 10% (moderate resizing), with a sharp cliff past it.

Noise
- Accuracy is bit-identical per recipe; time repeats within 0.1-2%.
- Any kernel or RNG-path change reshuffles accuracy by about ±0.2 pp.
- Seed std is about 0.25 pp, so the 3-seed mean std is about 0.15 pp.
- The tip has about an 85% chance of a 40-seed mean of at least 0.75.

Unsure
- Held-out seed offset.
- Whether the augment host stall is 0.1 s or 0.3 s under the 4-CPU pin.
- Whether any retune (Muon lr, LS, warm-up) hides +0.3 pp, which would buy back 0.5-1 epoch (about 5-10% time). That is now the main remaining lever besides systems work.

forecasts.reason: The run is GPU-bound at about 26 ms per step and Muon is already compiled, so graphs save only 0-4%. Capture complexity (conditional EMA, 3 pools) and max-autotune slowdown risk could also make it slower.
A larger angular step in a 238-step run with EMA is likely neutral to slightly negative. About a 30% chance of a +0.3 pp gain.
Muon weights are renormalized and have no wd term, so wd touches only the BN biases and head. The result is a ±0.2 pp reshuffle.
There are few true graph breaks. The only real stall is the masked-copy augment, about 0.1-0.2 s, so the gain is likely below or near the 3% bar.
Plain EMA loses the Lookahead reset's variance damping of the fast trajectory. The short final window gives little averaging, so I expect a 0.1-0.5 pp loss.

cruxes: What fraction of wall time is the GPU idle (host stalls from the masked-copy augment, eager SGD launches)? Above 5% would make systems work worth more than any retune.
Do held-out seeds 3-12 sit below the seeds 0-2 mean of 0.7548? If so, the tip is already fragile and no epoch cut is safe.
Does any optimizer or schedule retune (Muon lr, warm-up length, LS) add at least 0.3 pp? That is the only way to buy back 0.5-1 epoch.
